findings: No candidate tests or candidate VERB execution were run or seen by this reviewer. The candidate and its frozen inputs remain unchanged; this is a pre-proof static prediction, not validation.

The production change in isolated lib/run.js:42-49 destroys both captured output streams after the existing stop/termination attempt. Once an already-exited launcher has no captured pipe handles left, Node can deliver the child close event without waiting for its detached descendant's pipe ownership to end. This directly addresses the reproduced bounded-wait defect.

The timeout or output-limit error is recorded before stream closure, already collected output buffers are retained, and normal command completion never calls the added stream-destruction path. The common runSide error handling should therefore keep timed-out setup inconclusive and prevent the probe from running afterward.

The regression covers both stdout and stderr retained by a finite detached worker, an active-root timeout, and complete output from an ordinary successful command. Worker cleanup uses the fixture's own recorded PID and its working directory is outside the disposable source snapshot.

The author explicitly bounds this change to pipe draining, not reliable termination of escaped descendants or hard real-time cancellation. The existing synchronous Windows taskkill attempt can still add bounded overhead before streams are closed; that is unchanged and consistent with the stated scope.

The 400 ms timeout and 1500 ms elapsed assertion are scheduling-sensitive under a heavily loaded host, especially with Windows taskkill overhead. This is an unexecuted test reliability risk, not a statically demonstrated correctness defect in the candidate.

No blocking issue was identified within the stated scope. I would approve before runtime proof, with predicted VERB verdict verified. This automated independent review must not be reported as human review or as having observed a passing candidate.
